notes: Each mutant is one textual patch against the pristine module source.
kind=defect     : a plausible bug; surviving it is a real gap in the image oracle.
kind=equivalent : changes code shape but provably preserves the rendered function;
surviving is the correct outcome and calibrates false positives.
kind=defect-subthreshold : a real defect whose photometric effect was
measured (tools/sensitivity.py) to stay under the 8-bit visibility
floor; survival is the expected, quantified outcome, not a pass.

mutants.title: slab entry starts at 1e-2, clipping hits near the ray origin
slab test drops the ta/tb swap for negative ray directions
mutants.find: if (ta > tb) { float tmp = ta; ta = tb; tb = tmp; }
mutants.replace: if (ta > tb) { ta = ta; tb = tb; }

mutants.title: slab rejection predicate inverted (t0 < t1)
t0 never advances to the slab entry, so behind-origin boxes hit at t=0
t1 never shrinks to the slab exit, keeping boxes the ray misses
aabb_hit reports the exit parameter t1 instead of entry t0
slab distances multiply by d instead of the reciprocal
parallel threshold 1e-8 raised to 1e-1, misclassifying shallow rays
split picks narrowest instead of widest axis (tree shape only; same hits)
mutants.equivalence_note: only changes which axis is cut, so the same set of boxes is partitioned differently; nearest-hit answers are identical (validated: tree path equals brute path)

mutants.title: centroid partition disabled; falls back to index-median split
mutants.equivalence_note: falls back to the count/2 split; still a valid spatial partition, nearest-hit answers identical

mutants.title: partition counts left prims but never swaps them into place
mutants.find:
Prim tmp = t->p[i]; t->p[i] = t->p[mid]; t->p[mid] = tmp;
            mid++;
mutants.replace:
Prim tmp = t->p[i]; t->p[i] = t->p[i]; t->p[mid] = tmp;

mutants.title: leaf capacity 2 -> 1; deeper tree, identical hits
mutants.equivalence_note: tree depth only; the same boxes are tested, in a different grouping

mutants.title: leaf capacity 2 -> 3; shallower tree, identical hits
mutants.equivalence_note: tree depth only; same boxes tested

mutants.title: internal node bounds never grown; empty boxes degenerate to accept-all, so the tree stops culling
mutants.find: for (int i = first; i < first + count; i++) aabb_grow(&n->box, &t->p[i].box);
mutants.replace: for (int i = first; i < first; i++) aabb_grow(&n->box, &t->p[i].box);
mutants.equivalence_note: an empty AABB (min=+1e30, max=-1e30) makes the slab test accept every ray, so traversal degenerates to testing all boxes: same hits, no culling

mutants.title: aabb_grow no longer expands maxima
every primitive reports id 0, so all boxes alias primitive 0
split compares y centroids on the z axis and vice versa (tree shape only)
mutants.equivalence_note: only reorders the partition of boxes between children; same hits

mutants.title: build reuses node slot 0 for every node instead of reserving
aabb_area guard loosened; area is unused by traversal
mutants.equivalence_note: aabb_area is not called by traversal or by the renderer; no observable path

mutants.title: Lambert divides by pi; mutant multiplies by pi
mutants.find: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo / 3.14159265f; }
mutants.replace: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo * 3.14159265f; }

mutants.title: Lambert normalization by pi removed
mutants.find: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo / 3.14159265f; }
mutants.replace: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo; }

mutants.title: pi replaced by 3.16 (~0.6% dimming); below the measured 8-bit sensitivity floor
mutants.find: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo / 3.14159265f; }
mutants.replace: static float brdf_lambert(float albedo) { return albedo / 3.16f; }

mutants.title: cosine pdf normalization by pi removed
mutants.find: static float cosine_pdf(float cos_theta) { return cos_theta / 3.14159265f; }
mutants.replace: static float cosine_pdf(float cos_theta) { return cos_theta; }

mutants.title: pdf uses sin instead of cos, breaking the estimator weight
mutants.find: static float cosine_pdf(float cos_theta) { return cos_theta / 3.14159265f; }
mutants.replace: static float cosine_pdf(float cos_theta) { return sqrtf(1.0f - cos_theta * cos_theta) / 3.14159265f; }

mutants.title: cosine sampler uses u1 instead of sqrt(u1) for the radius
sampler z uses sqrt(u1) instead of sqrt(1-u1), collapsing to a cone
mutants.find: V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), sqrtf(1.0f - u1 > 0 ? 1.0f - u1 : 0) };
mutants.replace: V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), sqrtf(u1 > 0 ? u1 : 0) };

mutants.title: sampler azimuth spans pi instead of 2*pi
cosine_sample returns v unnormalized; |v| = 1 by construction
mutants.find:
V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), sqrtf(1.0f - u1 > 0 ? 1.0f - u1 : 0) };
    return norm3(v);
mutants.replace:
V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), sqrtf(1.0f - u1 > 0 ? 1.0f - u1 : 0) };
    return v;
mutants.equivalence_note: r^2 + (1-u1) = 1 exactly, so the sample is already unit length

mutants.title: norm3 loses its zero-length guard; no zero vectors reach it
mutants.find: if (l > 0) { r.x = a.x / l; r.y = a.y / l; r.z = a.z / l; }
mutants.replace: r.x = a.x / l; r.y = a.y / l; r.z = a.z / l;
mutants.equivalence_note: no zero-length vector reaches norm3 in these scenes (all inputs are ray directions or surface normals with |v|>0)

mutants.title: sampler emits negative z (below the shading hemisphere)
mutants.find: V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), sqrtf(1.0f - u1 > 0 ? 1.0f - u1 : 0) };
mutants.replace: V3 v = { r * cosf(phi), r * sinf(phi), -sqrtf(1.0f - u1 > 0 ? 1.0f - u1 : 0) };
